In the diagram below, $|PQ| = |PS|$ and $|QS| = |SR|$. If $\angle QRS = 40^\circ$, find the measure of $\angle PQS$:
questions.hint: $\triangle QSR$ is isosceles with base angles equal to $40^\circ$. Exterior angle $\angle PSQ = 40^\circ + 40^\circ = 80^\circ$. In isosceles $\triangle PQS$, base angles at $Q$ and $S$ are equal.
questions.workedSolution:
In $\triangle QSR$, $\vert{}QS\vert{} = \vert{}SR\vert{} \implies \angle SQR = \angle SRQ = 40^\circ$.
Exterior angle $\angle PSQ = 40^\circ + 40^\circ = 80^\circ$.
In $\triangle PQS$, $\vert{}PQ\vert{} = \vert{}PS\vert{} \implies \angle PQS = \angle PSQ = 50^\circ$ (or apex angle $P = 180^\circ - 2(50^\circ) = 80^\circ$).
Thus, $\angle PQS = 50^\circ$.

paper2.title: Paper 2: Essay / Theory Test (Variant)
paper2.instructions: Answer four questions only. All questions carry equal marks. All working must be clearly shown.

subQuestions.prompt: Given that $X = \{\text{whole numbers from } 5 \text{ to } 15\}$ and $Y = \{\text{multiples of } 3 \text{ between } 4 \text{ and } 22\}$, find $X \cap Y$.
Find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of 4, 6, and 10.
subQuestions.workedSolution:
Express each number as a product of prime factors:
$$4 = 2^2, \quad 6 = 2 \times 3, \quad 10 = 2 \times 5$$
Take the product of the highest powers of all prime factors:
$$\text{LCM} = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5 = 4 \times 3 \times 5 = 60$$.

Multiply through by the LCM of denominators (12):
$$12\left(\frac{3x + 4}{4}\right) + 12\left(\frac{x - 2}{3}\right) = 12(-1)$$
$$3(3x + 4) + 4(x - 2) = -12$$
$$9x + 12 + 4x - 8 = -12$$
$$13x + 4 = -12$$
$$13x = -12 - 4 = -16 \implies x = -\frac{16}{13} \quad \left(\text{or } -1\frac{3}{13}\right)$$.

subQuestions.prompt:
The ratio of boys to girls in a school is $11 : 20$. If there are 110 boys:
(i) How many girls are in the school?
(ii) What is the total enrolment of boys and girls in the school?
subQuestions.workedSolution:
(i) Let 1 ratio part be $k$:
$$11k = 110 \implies k = 10$$
$$\text{Number of girls} = 20 \times 10 = 200\text{ girls}$$

(ii) $$\text{Total enrolment} = 110 + 200 = 310\text{ students}$$.
*(Or $(11 + 20) \times 10 = 31 \times 10 = 310$)*.

Multiply numerical coefficients and apply the product law of indices:
$$\left(6 \times \frac{2}{3}\right) \times (a^2 \times a) \times (b^3 \times b^4)$$
$$= 4 \times a^{2+1} \times b^{3+4}$$
$$= 4a^3b^7$$.

(i) Let the number who passed Social Studies only be $y$.
Then the number who passed English Language only is $y + 10$.
$$\text{Total} = (\text{Social Studies only}) + (\text{Both}) + (\text{English only})$$
$$y + 20 + (y + 10) = 70$$
$$2y + 30 = 70 \implies 2y = 40 \implies y = 20$$
$$\text{Passed Social Studies} = 20 + 20 = 40\text{ candidates}$$
$$\text{Passed English Language} = (20 + 10) + 20 = 30 + 20 = 50\text{ candidates}$$

(ii) Candidates passing exactly one subject:
$$20 + 30 = 50\text{ candidates}$$
$$P(\text{exactly one subject}) = \frac{50}{70} = \frac{5}{7}$$.

subQuestions.prompt: Express 225% as a common fraction in its lowest terms.
In the diagram below, the interior apex angle of the triangle is $102^\circ$. Find the value of $x$:
subQuestions.workedSolution:
The interior base angles on the straight lines are:
$$\text{Left interior angle} = 180^\circ - 4x^\circ$$
$$\text{Right interior angle} = 180^\circ - 2x^\circ$$
The three interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^\circ$:
$$(180 - 4x) + (180 - 2x) + 102 = 180$$
$$462 - 6x = 180$$
$$6x = 462 - 180 = 282$$
$$x = \frac{282}{6} = 47$$
Thus, $x = 47$.

Evaluate the expression inside the brackets first:
$$\frac{10}{27} \div \frac{5}{9} = \frac{10}{27} \times \frac{9}{5} = \frac{2}{3}$$
Perform the outer division:
$$3 \div \frac{2}{3} = 3 \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{9}{2} = 4\frac{1}{2}$$.

subQuestions.prompt:
The table below represents a linear relation between $x$ and $y$: | x | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | y | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 | (i) Using a scale of 2 cm to 1 unit on the x-axis and 2 cm to 2 units on the y-axis, plot the points $(x, y)$ on a graph sheet for $1 \le x \le 5$ and $0 \le y \le 10$.
(ii) Join the plotted points with a straight line.
(iii) From your graph:

Find the gradient of the line and write down the equation of the line.
subQuestions.workedSolution:
(i) & (ii) Axes calibrated with given scale. Points $(1, 1), (2, 3), (3, 5), (4, 7), (5, 9)$ plotted accurately and connected by a continuous ruler-drawn straight line.

(iii) Choose two points, e.g., $(1, 1)$ and $(2, 3)$:
$$\text{Gradient } m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{3 - 1}{2 - 1} = 2$$
Using point-slope form with $(1, 1)$:
$$y - 1 = 2(x - 1) \implies y - 1 = 2x - 2 \implies y = 2x - 1$$
Equation of the line: $$y = 2x - 1$$.

subQuestions.prompt: Simplify: $$16 \times 8 \times 4 \times 2$$, leaving your answer in the form $2^n$.
subQuestions.workedSolution:
Express each term as a power of 2:
$$16 = 2^4, \quad 8 = 2^3, \quad 4 = 2^2, \quad 2 = 2^1$$
Apply the product law of indices:
$$2^4 \times 2^3 \times 2^2 \times 2^1 = 2^{4+3+2+1} = 2^{10}$$
Thus, $n = 10$, so the answer is $$2^{10}$$.

subQuestions.prompt:
The scores obtained by 25 pupils in a class test were:
$$3, 7, 6, 5, 6, 2, 1, 6, 3, 6, 4, 6, 5, 3, 4, 6, 5, 2, 6, 2, 5, 3, 7, 4, 2$$
Construct a frequency distribution table for the data.

subQuestions.workedSolution:
(i) Mode is the score with the highest frequency ($f = 7$):
$$\text{Mode} = 6$$

(ii) For $N = 25$, the median is the 13th score.
Cumulative frequencies: Score 1: 1; Score 2: 5; Score 3: 9; Score 4: 12; Score 5: 16.
Since the 13th score falls into the group of Score 5:
$$\text{Median} = 5$$

(iii) Mean score:
$$\text{Mean } (\bar{x}) = \frac{\sum fx}{\sum f} = \frac{109}{25} = 4.36$$.
